source_risks.title: Squared-error decomposition conditions
source_risks.detail: Opening every-model-error statement is broader than the later squared-loss derivation. Conditional mean f(x), independent test noise/fit, expectation domain and noise assumptions matter; a realized finite error is not universally lower-bounded by sigma^2.

source_risks.title: Capacity, bias and variance generalizations
source_risks.detail: Fixed capacity does not force every improvement in one component to worsen the other. High variance is not definitionally noise fitting; degree20 interpolation requires enough distinct data and appropriate solution assumptions. Source universal statements retained.

source_risks.title: Regularization effects and intercept exception
source_risks.detail: Increasing regularization does not universally increase bias/decrease variance in all settings. Ridge coefficient-wise shrinkage, L1 exact zeros and dropout interpretation require context; document fit explicitly excludes intercept from penalty.

source_risks.title: Double descent and implicit preference
source_risks.detail: Double descent is a possible behavior, not a universal guaranteed curve or complete explanation of generalization. Parameter count threshold p~n, simplest solution selection and peak persistence under regularization are conditional.

source_risks.title: Diagnostic heuristics and use of test set
source_risks.detail: Training/validation gaps alone do not identify population bias/variance; optimization failure, noise and distribution shift can also matter. More-data-is-useless and ship-it rules are strong source heuristics. Repeated diagnostics should not be mistaken for independent final test estimation.

source_risks.title: Ensemble variance and bias summaries
source_risks.detail: sigma^2/N requires equal variances and independence; correlated models need covariance terms. Bagging/boosting/stacking effects are not unconditional. Random forests add feature randomization beyond simple bagging. Source reduction less-than1/N phrasing ambiguous but faithfully retained.

source_risks.title: Bootstrap versus fresh population draws and finite estimates
source_risks.detail: generate_data draws new uniform/noisy data, not resamples from a fixed empirical training set. Source uses bootstrap terminology across these experiments. Known true function still leaves population bias/variance estimated from finite runs rather than exactly known.

source_risks.title: total_error is error against noise-free truth
source_risks.detail: Source code computes squared difference to y_true. Finite fixture gives bias_sq1 + variance2/3 = total_error5/3 exactly (roundoff), while adding example noise variance .25 gives1.9167, not the computed1.6667. Source prose says +noise; retained unchanged.

source_risks.title: Incomplete executable context
source_risks.detail: Original first generator call raises NameError np. Reviewer then supplied installed NumPy externally without editing source. Prediction/truth arrays supplied for b0153. Learning-curve call stops at missing predict_polynomial; regularization-sweep call stops at missing bias_variance_decomposition. x_test/y_test also need surrounding context. These snippet failures do not establish canonical failure; canonical was not read or run.

source_risks.title: Polynomial conditioning and lambda domain
source_risks.detail: Unscaled powers and normal equations can be ill-conditioned at high degree. Negative lambda silently follows least-squares branch; mismatched x/y lengths raise LinAlgError. A finite alpha100 need not force a degree15 polynomial on [-3,3] to constant; limiting behavior and basis scale differ.

source_risks.title: External library and compute-time claims
source_risks.detail: sklearn imports skipped under allowlist. Cross-validation learning/validation curves do not directly measure population decomposition. Negative-MSE sign, X/y dependencies and full timing/performance claims preserved; no external compatibility benchmark or10-15-minute result claimed.

source_risks.title: Exercise true-function mismatch
source_risks.detail: Exercise asks to change true function from polynomial to sin(x), but the earlier source generator already uses sin(1.5x)+0.5x. No silent correction in Chinese.

source_risks.title: Visual, artifact and execution limits
source_risks.detail: Five Mermaid payloads and figure bias-variance preserved. No actual diagrams rendered by reviewer. Exercises and output prompt not executed; all four references retained without outside research. Source strengths/limitations remain independent from translation approval.
